q.s: A 74-year-old woman falls onto her right shoulder. X-ray shows a fracture of the surgical neck of the humerus. On examination she cannot lift her arm away from her side beyond a few degrees, and the shoulder looks flattened. She has numbness over the lateral upper arm.
e: Wrong. Midshaft fracture with the radial nerve.
Wrong. Paired with the long thoracic nerve.
Wrong. Supracondylar fracture with the median nerve.
Correct. The axillary nerve and posterior circumflex humeral artery wind around the surgical neck.
cl: fracture of the surgical neck of the humerus
Classic site of axillary nerve injury.
numbness over the lateral upper arm
cannot lift her arm away from her side beyond a few degrees
Loss of abduction beyond 15° (supraspinatus still works).
q.ch: Surgical neck fracture → axillary nerve (deltoid, lateral arm) → posterior circumflex humeral artery.
q.tr: Humerus fractures follow the ARM: Axillary (neck), Radial (shaft), Median (supracondylar).
q.q2: Which artery is most likely to be injured along with the affected nerve?

q.s: A 28-year-old man has a midshaft humerus fracture after a motorcycle crash. He cannot extend his wrist or fingers, and has numbness over the dorsum of the hand between the thumb and index finger. Elbow extension against resistance is normal.
o: The median nerve supplies the triceps
The branches to the triceps leave the radial nerve above the spiral groove
The fracture is above the axilla
The injury is to the posterior interosseous nerve only
The triceps is innervated by the axillary nerve
e: Correct. Midshaft fractures spare triceps function and posterior arm sensation.
Wrong. Sensory loss indicates a more proximal lesion.
cl: Radial nerve in the spiral groove.
cannot extend his wrist or fingers
numbness over the dorsum of the hand
Elbow extension against resistance is normal
q.ch: Midshaft fracture → radial nerve in spiral groove → wrist drop + dorsal hand numbness, triceps spared.
q.tr: Crutch/axilla injury loses the triceps; midshaft injury spares it.
q.q2: Why is elbow extension preserved?

q.s: A 7-year-old girl falls from monkey bars onto her outstretched hand. X-ray shows a supracondylar fracture of the humerus. When asked to make a fist, her index and middle fingers remain extended. She cannot feel touch over the palmar thumb and index finger.
e: Correct. Proximal median nerve lesion: loss of thenar muscles, lateral lumbricals and long finger flexors ("hand of benediction").
cl: her index and middle fingers remain extended
cannot feel touch over the palmar thumb and index finger
q.ch: Supracondylar fracture → proximal median nerve → benediction sign on fist + lateral palm numbness → loss of opposition (LOAF).
q.tr: Median nerve: LOAF — Lateral 2 lumbricals, Opponens, Abductor, Flexor pollicis brevis.
q.q2: Which other function is most likely impaired?

q.s: A 45-year-old cyclist has numbness of his little finger and the ulnar half of his ring finger after a 300-km ride. He has weakness spreading his fingers apart. Sensation on the dorsal ulnar hand is normal. Flexion of the wrist is normal.
o: Lower trunk of the brachial plexus
e: Correct. The dorsal cutaneous branch leaves before the wrist, so dorsal sensation is spared.
Wrong. Would involve more than the ulnar nerve.
Wrong. Would weaken wrist flexion and affect the dorsal ulnar hand.
cl: Handlebar pressure on the hypothenar wrist.
Sensation on the dorsal ulnar hand is normal
Flexion of the wrist is normal
q.ch: Cyclist + ulnar sensory loss on palm + intrinsic weakness + spared dorsal sensation and FCU → ulnar nerve in Guyon canal.
q.tr: Distal ulnar lesions cause worse clawing than proximal ones ("ulnar paradox").
q.q2: Where is the nerve most likely compressed?

q.s: A newborn delivered after a difficult shoulder dystocia lies with the right arm hanging by his side, internally rotated, with the elbow extended and the forearm pronated. The grasp reflex in the right hand is present. The Moro reflex is absent on the right.
e: Correct. Erb palsy (C5–C6): loss of elbow flexion and supination.
cl: Lateral traction on the neck stretches the upper trunk.
the elbow extended and the forearm pronated
The grasp reflex in the right hand is present
q.ch: Shoulder dystocia → upper trunk C5–C6 → "waiter's tip" (adducted, internally rotated, extended, pronated) → biceps weakness.
q.tr: "Herb gets DIBs on tips": Deltoid, Infraspinatus, Biceps.
q.q2: Which muscle weakness explains the extended and pronated forearm?

q.s: A 34-year-old man grabbed a tree branch to stop a fall from a ladder. Since then, he has weakness of all intrinsic hand muscles with clawing of the fingers. His left eyelid droops and his left pupil is small.
e: Correct. Klumpke palsy; T1 involvement interrupts sympathetic fibers, causing Horner syndrome.
cl: weakness of all intrinsic hand muscles
His left eyelid droops and his left pupil is small
q.ch: Upward arm traction → lower trunk C8–T1 → claw hand + Horner syndrome.
q.tr: "Clawmpke" palsy.
q.q2: Which roots are injured?

q.s: A 52-year-old woman had a right mastectomy with axillary lymph node dissection 2 weeks ago. When she pushes against a wall, the medial border of her right scapula lifts off the chest wall. She cannot raise her right arm above her head.
e: Correct. Long thoracic nerve (C5–C7) injury causes winged scapula.
cl: Long thoracic nerve runs along the lateral chest wall.
the medial border of her right scapula lifts off the chest wall
cannot raise her right arm above her head
q.ch: Axillary dissection → long thoracic nerve → serratus anterior → winged scapula, no abduction above horizontal.
q.tr: Abduction >90° needs Serratus Anterior and Trapezius ("SALT": Serratus Anterior, Long Thoracic).
q.q2: Which muscle is paralyzed?

q.s: A 21-year-old man falls on his outstretched hand while skateboarding. He has pain and tenderness in the anatomic snuffbox. Wrist x-rays taken that day are normal.
o: Immediate surgical fixation for all cases
Immobilize in a thumb spica splint and repeat imaging (or obtain MRI)
Start NSAIDs and return to sports
e: Wrong. Scaphoid fractures are often occult.
Correct. Scaphoid fractures risk avascular necrosis and nonunion because of retrograde blood supply.
cl: x-rays taken that day are normal
q.ch: FOOSH + snuffbox tenderness + normal x-ray → presumed scaphoid fracture → immobilize and reimage (AVN risk).
q.tr: Treat snuffbox tenderness as a scaphoid fracture until proven otherwise.
q.q2: Which of the following is the most appropriate management?

q.s: A 30-year-old woman at 32 weeks' gestation has burning and tingling of her right thumb, index and middle fingers that wakes her at night. Shaking her hand relieves it. Holding her wrists in full flexion reproduces the symptoms. Sensation over the thenar eminence is normal.
o: The ulnar nerve supplies the thenar skin
The radial nerve supplies the thenar skin
The recurrent branch carries thenar sensation
The palmar cutaneous branch of the median nerve passes superficial to the carpal tunnel
cl: Holding her wrists in full flexion reproduces the symptoms
q.ch: Pregnancy + nocturnal median paresthesias + positive Phalen + spared thenar sensation → carpal tunnel syndrome.
q.tr: Thenar muscles may waste in carpal tunnel, but thenar skin sensation is spared.
q.q2: Why is sensation over the thenar eminence preserved?

q.s: A 58-year-old house painter has right shoulder pain when reaching overhead. He has pain and weakness when he abducts his arm with the thumbs pointing down and the arm held forward at 30°. External rotation strength is normal.
cl: thumbs pointing down and the arm held forward at 30°
q.ch: Overhead work + positive empty can + normal external rotation → supraspinatus → suprascapular nerve.
q.tr: Rotator cuff "SItS"; supraspinatus is the most commonly injured.
q.q2: Which nerve supplies the injured muscle?

q.s: A 22-year-old soccer player is struck on the outside of his left knee while his foot is planted. He has immediate pain and swelling. With the knee bent to 90°, the tibia can be pulled forward on the femur. Applying an outward force to the lower leg with the knee slightly bent widens the medial joint line.
e: Correct. "Unhappy triad" (ACL, MCL, meniscus); lateral meniscal tears are more common with ACL/MCL injuries.
Wrong. Classic teaching, but lateral involvement is more common.
cl: struck on the outside of his left knee while his foot is planted
the tibia can be pulled forward on the femur
q.ch: Lateral blow with planted foot → ACL + MCL ± meniscus (lateral more common than medial).
q.tr: Valgus stress test = MCL; varus = LCL.
q.q2: Which meniscus is most commonly injured along with these ligaments?

q.s: A 40-year-old man has a tight cast for a fibular neck fracture. He cannot lift his foot or turn it outward, and drags his toes when he walks. He has numbness over the top of the foot.
e: Correct. Common peroneal nerve injury: foot drop; "PED" (Peroneal Everts and Dorsiflexes).
cl: Common peroneal nerve wraps the fibular neck.
cannot lift his foot or turn it outward
numbness over the top of the foot
q.ch: Fibular neck injury + foot drop + loss of eversion + dorsal foot numbness → common peroneal nerve → steppage gait.
q.tr: "PED" foot gets dropPED; "TIP" — tibial can't stand on TIPtoes.
q.q2: Which gait abnormality will he use to clear the foot?

q.s: A 60-year-old woman received an intramuscular injection in the superomedial quadrant of her left buttock. Now, when she stands on her left leg, her right hip drops. When she stands on her right leg, her pelvis stays level.
e: Wrong. The pelvis is level when standing on the right.
Wrong. Inferior gluteal nerve; hip extension.
Correct. Superior gluteal nerve injury on the stance side (Trendelenburg sign).
cl: superomedial quadrant of her left buttock
Injection site risking the superior gluteal nerve.
when she stands on her left leg, her right hip drops
When she stands on her right leg, her pelvis stays level
q.ch: Superomedial gluteal injection → left superior gluteal nerve → weak left gluteus medius/minimus → right hip drops when standing on left.
q.tr: The lesion is on the side of the standing leg, opposite the dropping hip.
q.q2: Which muscle is weak?

q.s: A 46-year-old warehouse worker has sharp low back pain radiating down the back of his right leg to the sole of his foot after lifting a heavy box. He has difficulty walking on his toes, and his right ankle jerk is absent. Raising his straightened right leg reproduces the pain.
e: Correct. Compresses the S1 root (plantarflexion, Achilles reflex).
cl: radiating down the back of his right leg to the sole of his foot
his right ankle jerk is absent
Raising his straightened right leg reproduces the pain
q.ch: Posterolateral L5–S1 herniation → S1 root → toe walking difficulty + absent Achilles reflex.
q.tr: The root affected is usually the one below the disc level.
q.q2: Which disc level is most likely herniated?

q.s: A 64-year-old man who smokes has 3 months of difficulty climbing stairs and rising from a chair, a dry mouth and constipation. His strength briefly improves after sustained effort. Knee and ankle reflexes are absent but appear after 10 seconds of maximal contraction. Results of high-frequency repetitive nerve stimulation are shown.
o: Chest CT for small cell lung cancer
e: Wrong. Reflexes and autonomic signs point to LEMS.
Correct. Lambert-Eaton syndrome: antibodies to presynaptic voltage-gated Ca2+ channels; low baseline CMAP that increments with high-frequency stimulation.
cl: difficulty climbing stairs and rising from a chair
appear after 10 seconds of maximal contraction
q.ch: Smoker + proximal weakness improving with use + hyporeflexia + autonomic signs + incremental CMAP (figure) → LEMS → search for small cell lung cancer.
q.tr: Myasthenia: worse with use, decremental response; LEMS: better with use, incremental response.
q.q2: Which of the following is the most important next step?
q.fc: Compound muscle action potential during high-frequency stimulation

q.s: A 70-year-old thin woman who smokes and has taken prednisone for COPD for 6 years has sudden mid-back pain after bending to lift a laundry basket. She has lost 4 cm in height. Her laboratory and imaging results are shown.
o: Fibrous replacement of bone from high PTH
Bone resorption exceeding formation with normal mineralization
Disordered remodeling with increased osteoblast activity
e: Correct. Osteoporosis: normal labs, low T-score, fragility fracture; risk factors include age, low estrogen, smoking, glucocorticoids and low BMI.
Wrong. Myeloma; would raise calcium or protein.
Wrong. Osteomalacia; Ca/PO4 low, ALP high.
cl: taken prednisone for COPD for 6 years
bending to lift a laundry basket
q.ch: Risk factors + fragility vertebral fracture + T-score ≤ −2.5 + normal Ca, PO4, ALP, PTH (table) → osteoporosis.
q.tr: Osteoporosis has normal labs; if the labs are abnormal, look for another bone disease.
q.q2: Which of the following best explains her bone disease?

q.s: A 72-year-old man has a dull ache in both thighs and has noticed that his hats no longer fit. His hearing has declined. His legs appear bowed. His laboratory results are shown.
o: Avascular necrosis of the femoral head only
e: Correct. Paget disease of bone: isolated high ALP; AV shunts in bone and malignant transformation.
q.ch: Older man + enlarging skull + hearing loss + bowing + isolated high ALP with normal Ca/PO4/PTH (table) → Paget disease → osteosarcoma, high-output heart failure.
q.tr: "Hat size up, hearing down, ALP up, everything else normal" = Paget.
q.q2: This patient is at increased risk of which complication?

q.s: An 18-month-old boy who is exclusively breastfed and rarely goes outside has bowed legs and delayed walking. Examination shows a soft skull and beadlike swellings along the costochondral junctions. His laboratory results are shown.
o: Secondary hyperparathyroidism increases renal phosphate excretion
Phosphate is incorporated into new bone
Increased dietary phosphate loss in stool only
e: Correct. Low vitamin D lowers calcium, raising PTH, which wastes phosphate.
cl: exclusively breastfed and rarely goes outside
Low vitamin D intake and sun exposure.
beadlike swellings along the costochondral junctions
q.ch: Vitamin D deficiency → low Ca → high PTH → low PO4 + high ALP (table) → rickets.
q.tr: Rickets: ↓Ca, ↓PO4, ↑ALP, ↑PTH.
q.q2: Why is serum phosphate low?

q.s: A 2-year-old boy has frequent fractures, pallor and recurrent infections. He has poor vision and an enlarged liver and spleen. Hemoglobin is 7.2 g/dL with nucleated red cells on smear. Skeletal x-rays show diffusely dense bones with a "bone-within-bone" appearance.
e: Correct. Osteopetrosis: osteoclasts derive from monocytes, so a marrow transplant provides functional osteoclasts.
cl: Cranial nerve compression from narrowed foramina.
q.ch: Brittle dense bones + marrow failure + cranial nerve palsies → osteopetrosis (osteoclast defect, e.g., carbonic anhydrase II) → marrow transplant.
q.tr: "Stone bone" fills the marrow → pancytopenia.
q.q2: Which treatment is potentially curative?

q.s: A 38-year-old woman with SLE has taken prednisone 40 mg daily for 2 years. She has 3 months of deep, aching right groin pain that worsens with walking. Hip x-ray is normal; MRI shows a wedge-shaped area of bone death in the femoral head.
o: It is supplied by the lateral circumflex femoral artery only
The femoral head is a watershed area supplied mainly by the medial circumflex femoral artery
It is supplied by the obturator artery alone
cl: Early AVN may not show on x-ray.
q.ch: Glucocorticoids + SLE → femoral head infarction (watershed, medial circumflex) → AVN.
q.tr: AVN causes: "CASTS Bend LEGS."
q.q2: Why is this location particularly vulnerable?

q.s: A 13-year-old obese boy has had a limp and aching pain in his left knee for 3 weeks. Knee examination is normal. Internal rotation of the left hip is limited and painful, and when his hip is flexed, the thigh rotates outward.
e: Correct. Obese adolescent; hip pathology often presents as knee pain.
Wrong. Knee exam would be abnormal.
cl: when his hip is flexed, the thigh rotates outward
q.ch: Obese adolescent + knee pain with normal knee + limited hip internal rotation → SCFE.
q.tr: Always examine the hip in a child with knee pain.
q.q2: Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

q.s: A 6-year-old boy has had a painless limp for 6 weeks. He is afebrile. Hip abduction and internal rotation are mildly limited. Initial x-ray is normal; MRI shows avascular necrosis of the femoral head. There is no history of trauma or steroid use.
e: Correct. Idiopathic AVN of the femoral head, ages 5–7, boys 4:1.
cl: avascular necrosis of the femoral head
q.ch: Boy aged 5–7 + insidious limp + normal early x-ray + AVN of femoral head, no other cause → Legg-Calvé-Perthes.
q.tr: Perthes = young boy; SCFE = obese adolescent.
q.q2: Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

q.s: A couple of average height have a newborn with short arms and legs, a large head with frontal bossing and normal trunk length. The father is 52 years old. The family pedigree is shown; the arrow marks the newborn.
o: A new gain-of-function FGFR3 mutation associated with advanced paternal age
Autosomal recessive inheritance from carrier parents
e: Correct. >85% of achondroplasia cases are sporadic.
cl: short arms and legs, a large head
q.ch: Unaffected parents + short-limbed newborn with large head + older father (pedigree shows a single affected child) → sporadic FGFR3 gain-of-function → achondroplasia.
q.tr: FGFR3 activation inhibits chondrocyte proliferation.
q.q2: Which of the following best explains the newborn's condition?

q.s: A 15-year-old boy has a 2-month history of increasing pain and swelling just above his right knee that wakes him at night. X-ray shows a destructive lesion in the distal femoral metaphysis with a "sunburst" pattern and elevation of the periosteum forming a triangle.
cl: elevation of the periosteum forming a triangle
q.ch: Adolescent + metaphyseal lesion near knee + sunburst + Codman triangle → osteosarcoma → RB1/Li-Fraumeni risk.
q.tr: "Osteocod swimming in the sun."
q.q2: Which history would most increase his risk of this tumor?

q.s: A 9-year-old boy has fever, weight loss and pain in his left thigh. X-ray shows a destructive lesion in the femoral diaphysis with layered periosteal new bone. Biopsy shows sheets of small, round, blue cells. CD99 staining is positive.
cl: sheets of small, round, blue cells
q.ch: Child + diaphyseal lesion + onion skin + small round blue cells → Ewing sarcoma → t(11;22) EWS-FLI1.
q.tr: "11 + 22 = 33," Patrick Ewing's jersey.
q.q2: Which genetic finding confirms the diagnosis?

q.s: A 32-year-old woman has 4 months of aching pain in her left knee. X-ray shows an eccentric, expansile lytic lesion with a "soap bubble" appearance in the distal femoral epiphysis extending to the subchondral bone. Her growth plates are closed.
e: Wrong. A marker of osteoclasts, not the driver.
Wrong. A decoy that blocks RANKL.
Correct. Giant cell tumor: RANKL-expressing stromal cells recruit osteoclastlike giant cells (denosumab can be used).
q.ch: Young woman + epiphyseal soap-bubble lesion after skeletal maturity → giant cell tumor → RANKL-expressing cells.
q.tr: Epiphysis before maturity = chondroblastoma; after maturity = giant cell tumor.
q.q2: The tumor's neoplastic cells express which molecule that drives osteoclast formation?

q.s: Three patients present with an acutely swollen joint. Synovial fluid results are shown.
e: Correct. Patient 1 has gout (negatively birefringent needles); a xanthine oxidase inhibitor lowers urate production.
cl: Fluid analysis distinguishes gout, CPPD and infection.
Comparison of crystal and septic arthritis.
q.ch: Patient 1: first MTP + negatively birefringent needles → gout → allopurinol for overproducers. (Patient 2: CPPD; patient 3: septic S. aureus arthritis.)
q.tr: Gout: needles, negative, yellow parallel. CPPD: rhomboid, positive, blue parallel.
q.q2: Which drug would be most appropriate for long-term prevention in patient 1 if he overproduces uric acid?

head: Finding
Patient 1 (first MTP)
Patient 2 (knee)
Patient 3 (knee)
rows: Needle-shaped, yellow when parallel to the compensator
Rhomboid, blue when parallel to the compensator

q.s: A 60-year-old woman with long-standing rheumatoid arthritis has recurrent pneumonia. Her spleen is enlarged. Hemoglobin is 9.8 g/dL, absolute neutrophil count is 600/mm³ and platelets are 110,000/mm³. Her hands show ulnar deviation and swan neck deformities.
e: Correct. "SANTA": Splenomegaly, Anemia, Neutropenia, Thrombocytopenia, Arthritis (rheumatoid).
q.ch: RA + splenomegaly + neutropenia (± anemia, thrombocytopenia) → Felty syndrome.
q.tr: Felty = SANTA.
q.q2: Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

q.s: A 20-year-old woman has fever, migratory pain in her wrists and ankles, painful swelling along the tendons of her right hand, and a few small pustules on her forearms. She has a new sexual partner.
e: Correct. Disseminated gonococcal infection: polyarthralgia, tenosynovitis and dermatitis.
cl: migratory pain in her wrists and ankles
painful swelling along the tendons of her right hand
q.ch: Young sexually active adult + polyarthralgia + tenosynovitis + pustules → disseminated gonococcal infection.
q.tr: DGI triad: arthralgia, tenosynovitis, dermatitis.
q.q2: Which of the following is the most likely causal organism?

q.s: A 26-year-old man has a painful, swollen right knee and left ankle 3 weeks after a bout of bloody diarrhea from undercooked chicken. He has red, irritated eyes and burning on urination. He has scaly, crusted lesions on his soles.
e: Correct. Reactive arthritis, a seronegative spondyloarthritis.
cl: scaly, crusted lesions on his soles
q.ch: Enteric infection → arthritis + conjunctivitis + urethritis + keratoderma → reactive arthritis → HLA-B27.
q.tr: "Can't see, can't pee, can't bend my knee."
q.q2: Which HLA type is most strongly associated with this condition?

q.s: A 27-year-old man has had low back pain and stiffness for 1 year that is worst in the morning and improves with exercise. Lumbar spine flexion is limited. Chest expansion is reduced. He had one episode of a painful red eye with light sensitivity.
e: Correct. Ankylosing spondylitis causes aortitis and AR.
cl: worst in the morning and improves with exercise
painful red eye with light sensitivity
q.ch: Young man + inflammatory back pain + reduced chest expansion + uveitis → ankylosing spondylitis → aortic regurgitation.
q.tr: AS: bamboo spine, uveitis, aortic regurgitation.
q.q2: Which cardiac complication is he at increased risk for?

q.s: A 24-year-old woman has fatigue, painful joints, a rash on her cheeks after sun exposure, and leg swelling. Urinalysis shows protein 3+ and red cell casts. Her autoantibody panel is shown.
e: Correct. SLE: accelerated atherosclerosis is the most common cause of death.
Wrong. Common, but not the most common.
Wrong. Common, but not the most common.
cl: rash on her cheeks after sun exposure
q.ch: Young woman + malar rash + arthritis + nephritis + anti-dsDNA, anti-Sm, low complement (table) → SLE → cardiovascular death.
q.tr: Anti-dsDNA tracks disease and nephritis activity; anti-Sm is most specific.
q.q2: Which of the following is the most common cause of death in patients with this disease?

q.s: A 32-year-old woman has had three pregnancy losses in the second trimester. She now has a swollen left calf from a deep vein thrombosis. PTT is prolonged and does not correct when mixed with normal plasma. A screening test for syphilis was positive, but a treponemal test is negative.
cl: three pregnancy losses in the second trimester
does not correct when mixed with normal plasma
q.ch: Recurrent pregnancy loss + thrombosis + prolonged PTT not corrected + false-positive VDRL → antiphospholipid syndrome → anticoagulation.
q.tr: Lupus anticoagulant prolongs PTT in the lab but causes clots in the patient.
q.q2: Which of the following is the most appropriate long-term treatment?

q.s: A 74-year-old woman has 2 months of aching and stiffness in both shoulders and hips, worst in the morning. Strength is normal. She now has a new left temporal headache and pain in her jaw when chewing. ESR is 96 mm/h and CK is normal.
o: Temporal artery biopsy before any treatment
Low-dose prednisone and follow up in 1 month
Start high-dose glucocorticoids immediately and arrange temporal artery biopsy
e: Wrong. Treats PMR, but GCA symptoms require high dose.
Correct. Giant cell arteritis threatens vision.
q.k: Polymyalgia rheumatica and giant cell arteritis
cl: aching and stiffness in both shoulders and hips
new left temporal headache and pain in her jaw when chewing
q.ch: PMR + new headache + jaw claudication + very high ESR → GCA → immediate high-dose steroids.
q.tr: Never delay steroids in suspected GCA; biopsy remains positive for days.
q.q2: Which of the following is the most appropriate immediate step?

q.s: A 56-year-old woman has 3 months of difficulty climbing stairs and lifting her arms to wash her hair. She has a purple discoloration of her upper eyelids and raised red scaly papules over her knuckles. CK is 4,200 U/L. Anti-Jo-1 is positive.
e: Correct. Dermatomyositis is associated with an increased risk of cancer.
cl: difficulty climbing stairs and lifting her arms
purple discoloration of her upper eyelids
red scaly papules over her knuckles
q.ch: Proximal weakness + heliotrope rash + Gottron papules + high CK + anti-Jo-1 → dermatomyositis → screen for malignancy.
q.tr: Dermatomyositis: perimysial, CD4+; polymyositis: endomysial, CD8+.
q.q2: Which of the following evaluations is most important?

q.s: A 2-year-old boy from Japan has had fever for 6 days. He has red eyes without discharge, cracked red lips, a red "strawberry" tongue, a spreading rash, a swollen lymph node in his neck, and red, swollen hands and feet.
e: Correct. Kawasaki disease; prevents coronary artery aneurysms.
cl: swollen lymph node in his neck
q.ch: Asian child + fever ≥5 days + CRASH features → Kawasaki → IVIG + aspirin to prevent coronary aneurysms.
q.tr: "CRASH and burn": Conjunctivitis, Rash, Adenopathy, Strawberry tongue, Hands/feet, burn (fever).
q.q2: Which of the following is the most appropriate treatment?

q.s: A 48-year-old man has chronic sinus congestion with bloody nasal crusts, a perforated nasal septum, cough with blood-streaked sputum and new leg swelling. Chest CT shows multiple cavitating nodules. Urinalysis shows red cell casts. Kidney biopsy shows a pauci-immune crescentic glomerulonephritis.
q.ch: Upper airway + lung nodules + pauci-immune RPGN → GPA → PR3-ANCA.
q.tr: GPA triad: upper respiratory, lungs, kidneys.
q.q2: Which antibody is most likely to be present?

q.s: A 70-year-old woman has painful erosions in her mouth for 2 months and now has large flaccid blisters on her trunk that break easily, leaving raw areas. Light rubbing of normal-looking skin causes it to slough. Biopsy shows separation of keratinocytes above the basal layer, which remains attached to the basement membrane.
o: Granular IgA at the tips of dermal papillae
Linear IgG and C3 along the basement membrane
Net-like IgG around keratinocytes throughout the epidermis
e: Correct. Pemphigus vulgaris: antibodies to desmoglein 3 (± 1).
cl: Light rubbing of normal-looking skin causes it to slough
basal layer, which remains attached to the basement membrane
q.ch: Older adult + oral erosions + flaccid bullae + Nikolsky positive + suprabasal acantholysis → pemphigus vulgaris → reticular IgG.
q.tr: Pemphigus: mouth involved, flaccid, Nikolsky +; pemphigoid: mouth spared, tense, Nikolsky −.
q.q2: Immunofluorescence of the biopsy would most likely show which pattern?

q.s: A 48-year-old fair-skinned man has a mole on his back that his wife says has grown over 6 months. It is 9 mm wide, asymmetric, with an irregular border and areas of black, brown and pink. Excisional biopsy shows atypical melanocytes invading to a depth of 2.8 mm.
e: Wrong. A diagnostic marker, not prognostic.
cl: 9 mm wide, asymmetric, with an irregular border
invading to a depth of 2.8 mm
q.ch: Changing pigmented lesion with ABCDE features → melanoma → Breslow depth predicts metastasis.
q.tr: ABCDE: Asymmetry, Border, Color, Diameter >6 mm, Evolution.
q.q2: Which feature of the biopsy best predicts the risk of metastasis?

q.s: A 35-year-old man is rescued from a house fire. He has burns over his entire right arm, the entire front of his chest and abdomen, and the front of his right leg. The burned skin is white, leathery and painless to pinprick. His voice is hoarse and there is soot in his mouth. The burn distribution is shown.
o: Full-thickness burns of about 36% of body surface; secure the airway because of inhalation injury
Deep partial-thickness of 18%; skin grafting first
e: Wrong. These burns are painless and leathery.
Correct. Hoarseness and soot indicate airway edema.
cl: white, leathery and painless to pinprick
q.ch: 9 + 18 + 9 = 36% (table) full-thickness burns + hoarseness and soot → inhalation injury → secure airway first.
q.tr: Airway first in burns with soot, singed nasal hair or hoarseness.
q.q2: What is the depth of his burns and the most urgent priority?
